sermon.title: Four Necessary but Risky Present Day Truths, Part 1
sermon.series: Four Necessary but Risky Present Day Truths
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer names four necessary but risky things, government, law enforcement, the military and the judicial system, and gives 20th-century figures and examples of governments killing innocent people. He then gives Bible examples of censoring God’s word, judicial injustice, murder by government and removing arms, and says God can use a moral generation to change evil laws.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the recording begins mid-sentence. He gives the Manasseh reference as “2 Kings 20:18 through 9”; the verses quoted are 2 Kings 21:8-9 (shown). He gives “Daniel 3:20” for the king saying their God “changed the king’s word,” which is Daniel 3:28 (shown). Where the captions place the Khmer Rouge “in Colombia,” the country is marked [unclear] (the Khmer Rouge ruled Cambodia). All statistics and historical statements in this message (the 20th-century death figures he cites from a 20th-century atlas, the refugee total, Rwanda, Guatemala, the Congo, China, Christians killed, the 1930s veterans’ protest, the New York police, the California marriage ruling and the judge, and the dates of court rulings) are his own and are not verified here; his comments about named political and religious figures, Islam in public schools and homosexuality are likewise his own. Several words are marked [unclear].

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now there was no blacksmith to be found throughout all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, “Lest the Hebrews make swords or spears.” But all the Israelites would go down to the Philistines to sharpen each man’s plowshare, his mattock, his ax, and his sickle; and the charge for a sharpening was a pim for the plowshares, the mattocks, the forks, and the axes, and to set the points of the goads. So it came about, on the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan. But they were found with Saul and Jonathan his son.

faqs.question: What are the four necessary but risky things he names?
faqs.answer: He names government, law enforcement, the military and the judicial system: necessary, but risky and dangerous.

faqs.question: What does the word democide mean?
faqs.answer: He says democide is a new word in the dictionary which means murder by government.

faqs.question: How many refugees does he count in the 20th century?
faqs.answer: He says he added up the refugees from 1900 to 2000 and it came to over 33 million people who had to leave their land because of persecution and oppression.

faqs.question: How many Christians does he say were killed for their faith in that century?
faqs.answer: He says nations killed 45 and a half million Christians “just because they were Christians,” and shows a picture of Christians being slaughtered in Iraq.

faqs.question: Who does he say should make laws?
faqs.answer: He says the constitution says Congress makes laws, the states have a right to make laws for their state, and judges are making laws instead.

faqs.question: What does it mean to censor the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says to censor means to criticize it, pay no attention to it, condemn it and denounce it.

faqs.question: What did Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego tell the king?
faqs.answer: He says they told the king God can deliver us, but if He doesn’t, “we’re not worship in your idols.”

faqs.question: What does he mean that God has a newspaper of His own?
faqs.answer: He says we just believe what’s going on in the news, but “God has a newspaper of his own that we need to learn how to read.”

faqs.question: How did Israel win a battle without swords?
faqs.answer: He says the rest of the army had axes, sickles, mattocks and plows to fight with, and because God was on their side they won the war.
